examples.questionText:
Suppose a study was done to look at the relationship between the number of hours per week online statistics students put into the class and their GPA.

Hours18414810201562
GPA3.92.13.32.72.93.53.42.21.3

a. Write down the null and alternative hypothesis.

b. Write down the test statistic and the p-value.

c. State the conclusion of the hypothesis test in the context of the study

d. Write down the equation of the regression line.

e. Interpret the slope of the regression line in the context of the study.

f. Interpret the y-intercept of the regression line in the context of the study or explain why it is not relevant.

g. Use the regression line to predict the GPA of a student who puts in 13 hours a week.

h. Interpret `r^2` in the context of the study.

keyPatterns: NO PHP control code — regression essay questions live entirely in qtext (pure HTML)
Data presented as HTML <table border='1'> with 2 rows: variable name + 9 numeric values

Standard 8-part structure: (a) H0/Ha → (b) test stat + p-value → (c) conclusion in context → (d) regression equation → (e) slope interpretation → (f) y-intercept interpretation or why irrelevant → (g) prediction → (h) r^2 interpretation
Real-world context: uses relatable paired variables (hours vs GPA, crime vs rent, screen time at work vs not)
Not Randomized — fixed datasets, not PHP-randomized
Empty answer field and empty scoremethod — pure manual grading
9 data points is the standard dataset size for this question type
patternSummary.suggestedApproach: Write qtext-only (no control code needed). Use <table border='1'> for data. Follow 8-part a-h structure. Pick real-world paired quantitative variables. Use exactly 9 data pairs. Include a specific prediction value in part g and r^2 interpretation in part h. No loadlibrary calls needed.
